summary.text: Marquita Bradshaw is a Memphis-born environmental-justice advocate and community organizer, and the Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate. She was the Democratic nominee for this seat in 2020, losing to Bill Hagerty, lost the 2024 Democratic Senate primary to Gloria Johnson, and won the 2026 primary. She is the founder and executive director of Sowing Justice.

paragraphs.text: Born January 12, 1974 and raised in Memphis, Tennessee; her parents helped organize residents around contamination at the Memphis Defense Depot Superfund site.
Earned a high school diploma from Central High School and a bachelor's degree from the University of Memphis (a Bachelor of Liberal Studies in journalism and communication studies, per Wikipedia).

Her career and advocacy work, according to her Ballotpedia survey, has spanned labor, environmental, education-reform, tax-reform, trade-policy and social-justice causes; she has worked as a caretaker for a differently abled adult and says she experienced medical bankruptcy.

Wikipedia reports she chairs the environmental justice committee of the Sierra Club's Tennessee chapter, and has worked with the Mid-South Peace and Justice Center, the AFL-CIO, the Sierra Club and Tennesseans for Fair Taxation.

Won the 2020 Democratic Senate primary with 35.5% in a five-candidate field, becoming the first Black woman nominated for statewide office by a major party in Tennessee, per Wikipedia. She lost the general election to Bill Hagerty, about 62% to 35%.
Founded Sowing Justice after the 2020 race, which she describes as a nonpartisan organization focused on civic engagement beyond voting; she serves as its executive director.
Lost the 2024 Democratic Senate primary to Gloria Johnson, then won the August 6, 2026 Democratic primary with 54.7% of the vote over four opponents.
